findings.title: upsampled_count sums raw sample_weight without a NULL fallback, undercounting events
findings.body:
`upsampled_count` compiles to `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Any error event without a `sample_weight` is effectively dropped from the count, because ClickHouse `sum` ignores NULLs. That includes events ingested before the project was allowlisted, events from SDKs that don't send `error_sampling` context, and events in an allowlisted project that weren't client-sampled.

Once a project is added to the allowlist, every chart that covers older data, or mixes sampled and unsampled events, shows a lower count than plain `count()` would. The comment says the code "assumes sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects", but nothing in ingestion guarantees that.

The aggregate should treat a missing weight as 1, e.g. `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`. The endpoint test only stores events that carry a sample rate, so it cannot catch this.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused
Upsampling decision uses the outer `dataset`/request query instead of `scoped_dataset`/`query`
findings.body:
`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check passes the outer `dataset`, and the helper reads `request.GET['query']`.

In the dashboard discover-split path, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` and an errors-only query such as `(...) AND !event.type:transaction`, or with the widget's `ERROR_EVENTS` split. Because the outer `dataset` there is `metrics_enhanced_performance`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False. Error counts from those split queries are therefore never upsampled, while the same widget on the errors dataset would be.

Conversely, the decision ignores the rewritten `split_query`. Pass `scoped_dataset` and `query` to the eligibility check.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache serves stale allowlist decisions and the invalidation hook is never called
findings.body:
Eligibility is cached per (org, project set) for 60 seconds. When a project is removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, queries keep returning upsampled counts for up to a minute, and the reverse is also true.

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere. It also cannot realistically be called on an allowlist change, because the cache key space is every combination of project IDs any user has queried.

This also contradicts the `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` docstring (lines 50-53), which says the allowlist is read "fresh each time ... to ensure we always have the latest configuration state".

findings.title: Added cache lookup is likely slower than the option read it replaces
findings.body:
The docstring justifies the cache as avoiding "expensive repeated option lookups". However, `options.get` is already served from an in-process cache, and the uncached work is a list membership check.

The new code adds a `cache.get`, plus a `cache.set` on miss, against the shared cache backend (Redis or memcached). That is a network round trip on every `_get_event_stats` call, and in the dashboard split and fallback paths there can be several calls per request.

This adds latency and load rather than removing it. Either drop the cache or rely on the options layer's existing caching.

findings.title: Cache key uses `hash()` of the project tuple, so different project sets can collide
findings.body:
The cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))` instead of the IDs or a cryptographic digest. Two different project sets in the same org that hash to the same value share a cache entry for 60s.

That can upsample a query over a non-allowlisted project set, or fail to upsample an allowlisted one. Use a stable digest such as md5 or sha1 of the joined sorted IDs if key length is the concern.

findings.title: Stray gitlink/submodule `sentry-repo` added to the repository
findings.body:
The PR adds a `sentry-repo` entry that is a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`, which is the base commit itself). There is no `.gitmodules` entry and it is unrelated to the feature.

It looks like an accidental commit of a nested checkout. It will confuse clones and submodule tooling and break `git submodule` operations, so it should be removed.

findings.title: Top-events ranking still uses raw count() while the series show upsampled counts
findings.body:
In the top-events path only `timeseries_columns` are rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count`. `selected_columns` (from `get_field_list`) and `orderby` (e.g. `-count()`) are left untouched.

The top N groups are therefore chosen by unweighted event count, while the plotted values are weighted counts. When client sample rates differ between groups, the ranking can disagree with the displayed values, and a group with a higher upsampled count can be excluded from the top N.

findings.title: No tests for the cached entry point or for negated/compound queries
findings.body:
The unit tests only exercise the private helpers. `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is never tested, so its cache hit/miss behaviour and staleness are uncovered. The `self.snuba_params` built in `setUp` is unused.

`_is_error_focused_query` is only checked against `event.type:error`, `event.type:transaction` and an empty query. A case such as `!event.type:error`, which currently returns True, would have exposed the substring-matching bug.

The endpoint tests also don't cover allowlisted projects containing events without `sample_weight`, which is where `sum(sample_weight)` undercounts.
